class.name: InputSettings
class.brief_description: Settings resource of [InputSettingsServer]: sensitivity, inversion, deadzone, vibration, toggle actions and the input options of the engine.
class.description: The data of the settings domain [code]"input"[/code]. [InputSettingsServer] keeps three copies of it (defaults, applied and pending values, see [method SettingsServer.get_settings]) and stores it in [code]user://settings/input.ini[/code]. Change the values through [InputSettingsServer] or [method SettingsServer.set_value], not on the resource, so that they are validated and applied. Only [member emulate_mouse_from_touch], [member emulate_touch_from_mouse] and [member use_accumulated_input] reach the engine ([Input]). All other values are game-side values: the engine stores them, and the game applies them through the helpers of [InputSettingsServer], for example [method InputSettingsServer.apply_to_mouse_motion]. It can also be used as the project defaults of the domain: save an [InputSettings] as a [code].tres[/code] file and name it in the project setting [code]settings/defaults/input[/code].

members.member: If [code]true[/code], keyboard, mouse and touch events belong to the first player (see [method InputSettingsServer.is_player_event]). Turn it off when the first player uses a gamepad and another player uses the keyboard.

If [code]true[/code], touch events also send mouse events (see [member Input.emulate_mouse_from_touch]). The default is the value the engine has when the domain starts, which comes from [member ProjectSettings.input_devices/pointing/emulate_mouse_from_touch].

If [code]true[/code], mouse events also send touch events (see [member Input.emulate_touch_from_mouse]). The default is the value the engine has when the domain starts, which comes from [member ProjectSettings.input_devices/pointing/emulate_touch_from_mouse].
The joypad device of the first player (see [member InputEvent.device]), or [code]-1[/code] for any joypad. Used by [method InputSettingsServer.is_player_event].
The radial deadzone of the look stick, from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]0.95[/code]. Used by [method InputSettingsServer.apply_to_stick].
The factor for the look stick of a gamepad, from [code]0.01[/code] to [code]10.0[/code].
If [code]true[/code], the horizontal look axis of a gamepad is inverted.
If [code]true[/code], the vertical look axis of a gamepad is inverted.
The factor for looking or turning with keys, from [code]0.01[/code] to [code]10.0[/code].
If [code]true[/code], the horizontal look axis of the keyboard is inverted.
If [code]true[/code], the vertical look axis of the keyboard is inverted.
If [code]true[/code], the cursor stays inside the window while it is visible (see [method InputSettingsServer.set_mouse_captured]).
The factor for mouse motion, from [code]0.01[/code] to [code]10.0[/code].
How much [method InputSettingsServer.apply_to_mouse_motion] blends a motion with the previous one, from [code]0.0[/code] (off) to [code]0.95[/code].
If [code]true[/code], the horizontal mouse axis is inverted.
If [code]true[/code], the vertical mouse axis is inverted.

The input actions that toggle instead of being held, for example [code]"crouch"[/code], [code]"sprint"[/code] or [code]"aim"[/code]. Empty names and duplicates are removed. Used by [method InputSettingsServer.is_action_active].
If [code]true[/code], similar input events in one frame are merged (see [member Input.use_accumulated_input]).
If [code]false[/code], [method InputSettingsServer.vibrate] does nothing.
The factor for the magnitudes passed to [method InputSettingsServer.vibrate], from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code].
